reason: The text contains an extended divine complaint from Yahweh (delivered through the prophetess Huldah) expressing displeasure with the people's unfaithfulness. Yahweh explicitly states they 'have forsaken me and have burned incense to other gods, to provoke me to anger with all the work of their hands' (תַחַת אֲשֶׁר עֲזָבוּנִי וַיְקַטְּרוּ לֵאלֹהִים אֲחֵרִים לְמַעַן הַכְּעִיסֵנִי). The text repeatedly emphasizes Yahweh's anger is 'kindled' against Judah and details His grievances about their idolatry and unfaithfulness. Additionally, the closing section reiterates that 'the Lord did not turn from the fierceness of his great anger, which was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations with which Manasseh had provoked him.' This constitutes a divine complaint—an expression of Yahweh's profound displeasure with the people's actions.
